newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma says may extend parliament's term.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma says may extend parliament's term.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma said on Friday he might extend parliament's term, due to expire in March 1998, by one year to "approve laws on the economy".
"I am ready to consider the question of extending parliament's duties by one year," Kuchma said in a speech at celebrations on the eve of the first anniversary of Ukraine's post-Soviet constitution.
Kuchma, speaking about two hours after the conservative-dominated chamber approved the 1997 budget six months into the year, said parliament would have its term extended to consider economic reforms.
"This period must be used to approve laws in the economic sphere," he declared, making clear he wanted deputies to have more time to approve reforms which they have tended to resist.

Kuchma, author of Ukraine's first economic reform programme in 1994, said he had no plans to postpone presidential elections due in October 1999. But regional administrative leaders elected in parallel with this parliament could have their terms extended, he said.

Parliament has been reluctant to accept reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund, which said on Friday it might issue Ukraine with another stand-by loan instead of a three-year, $2.5-$3 billion Extended Fund Facility intended for countries undertaking painful structural reforms.
